description:
Desktop client for openHPSDR Protocol 1/2 SDR radios.

A Rust/egui desktop client for openHPSDR Protocol 1 and Protocol 2 radios (Metis/Ozy-style and Hermes/Orion-style boards), using WDSP for DSP.

- Protocol 1 (Metis/Ozy) and Protocol 2 (Hermes/Orion) support, with standard openHPSDR UDP discovery
- Multiple simultaneous receivers, each with its own VFO, mode, filter width, and band memory
- Spectrum/waterfall display with adjustable dB range, palette, and Click-to-Tune (CTUN)
- SSB/CW/AM/FM/digital modes, per-mode/per-band filter width and mode memory
- Noise blanker (NB/NB2), noise reduction (NR/NR2/NNR), and SNB, independently switchable
- AGC with selectable Off/Long/Slow/Medium/Fast modes
- TX: mic audio through WDSP's TXA chain, ALC, TX power/SWR meter with per-band PA calibration, and a Tune button
- PureSignal (PA linearization/predistortion), on both Protocol 1 and Protocol 2
- rigctl (Hamlib-compatible), TCI (WebSocket), and CAT (Kenwood TS-2000 emulation) control servers
- Dual VFO (VFO A/B) with Split -- transmit on VFO B while receiving on VFO A
- Selectable RX output / TX input audio devices, independent of the OS default
- Per-radio settings persistence, keyed by the radio's MAC address
- FPGA firmware upload and static IP configuration
Changes since v0.12.1; see v0.12.0 for everything new in 0.12.
New
- UI Scale (Settings → Spectrum): makes the whole interface -- text, buttons and every window -- smaller or larger in 10% steps, on top of the desktop's own display scale, and keeps it for next time. Ctrl -, Ctrl + and Ctrl 0 do the same from any window. Useful where the desktop scales everything up, e.g. on a Raspberry Pi, and extra receivers don't fit on the screen.
- Theme (Settings → Spectrum): Dark (the default), Light, or Follow system -- dark or light as the computer is set, changing when it does (Windows, macOS, and Linux desktops such as GNOME and KDE). Every window follows it; the spectrum, waterfall and meters stay dark. Settings, Discovery and Firmware Update now follow the theme too, so they're dark in Dark, where they used to be always light.
- The web client follows the phone's, tablet's or browser's dark/light setting.
- Lost packets and audio gaps are now counted. If packets from the radio go missing on the way, or the audio runs dry, an orange Lost N packets / Audio gaps: N shows under the S-meter for a few seconds, and the log records it with the time. Settings → About shows the figures -- packets lost out of those sent, audio gaps, and when each last happened -- with a Reset, e.g. to compare Wi-Fi with a cable. If you've had stuttering audio or spectrum, these say whether it's the network or the audio.
Fixes
- Stuttering audio and spectrum on some Windows and Raspberry Pi 5 systems:
  - hpsdr-rs now asks for a 1 MB network receive buffer for the radio's data, as Thetis does, instead of the system's default (64 KB on Windows), which could lose packets at high sample rates or with several receivers. On Raspberry Pi OS the system allows only about 208 KB unless raised: sudo sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=1048576.
  - The audio now keeps about 50 ms queued, rather than playing the moment it arrives, so a late block from the radio, or a sound card that takes audio in large or uneven blocks (HDMI, Bluetooth), no longer makes a gap.
- Window sizes are saved and restored again on Wayland (the default on Linux since v0.8.4), where nothing was saved at all. Positions can't be restored on Wayland, which doesn't let programs place their windows; start with HPSDR_FORCE_X11=1 to have them restored as well.
Downloads
- Linux AppImage (x86_64 / aarch64): hpsdr-rs-0.12.2-x86_64.AppImage, hpsdr-rs-0.12.2-aarch64.AppImage. Run chmod +x on the file, then run it. USB radios still need the udev rules installed by hand; a copy is inside the AppImage under usr/share/doc/hpsdr-rs.
- Debian/Ubuntu (amd64): hpsdr-rs_0.12.2-1_amd64.deb. Install with sudo apt install ./hpsdr-rs_0.12.2-1_amd64.deb.
- Debian/Ubuntu/Raspberry Pi OS (arm64): hpsdr-rs_0.12.2-1_arm64.deb. Install with sudo apt install ./hpsdr-rs_0.12.2-1_arm64.deb.
- Fedora/openSUSE RPM (x86_64 / aarch64): hpsdr-rs-0.12.2-1.x86_64.rpm, hpsdr-rs-0.12.2-1.aarch64.rpm. Install with sudo dnf install ./hpsdr-rs-0.12.2-1.x86_64.rpm, or on openSUSE sudo zypper install --allow-unsigned-rpm ./hpsdr-rs-0.12.2-1.x86_64.rpm.
- macOS (Apple Silicon): hpsdr-rs-0.12.2-macos-arm64.tar.gz. It is built in CI, unsigned and not notarized, so Gatekeeper warns on first launch. Right-click the hpsdr-rs binary and choose Open, or run xattr -d com.apple.quarantine hpsdr-rs first.
- Windows (x86_64): hpsdr-rs-0.12.2-x86_64.msi
